name: base
purpose: 8 ns clock; power-up reset with a start request and a clock edge inside it; conversion of 0.60 V with vin moved to 0.20 V right after sampling (code 10); a start 2*tr plus one 50 ps grid step after the done edge (code 8, 5 mV above mid-scale); a busy start after two decisions re-arms (the first conversion never finishes, the second gives 13); inputs below vss and above vref (0 and 15) with sample_dbg showing the raw sample; a start held high across its done edge; a reset pulse between edges after two decisions with a start request inside it; a sample 5 mV above DAC(10); starts 2*tr plus a design margin after and before a clock edge (5 ps after an idle edge moved 5 ps early, one 50 ps grid step before a sample edge; a separation exactly at a contract minimum is a tie)

name: modules-default
purpose: each module on its own, default parameters: the DAC through all 16 codes with multi-bit changes; the comparator with the DAC input stepping across the sample by large amounts and by 2 to 10 mV; the sample-and-hold with sample_en changing 0.3 ns before and after edges, a slow input ramp, rst over an edge and between edges, inputs outside the range; the controller with decision patterns 1010, 1111, 0000, a start 100 ps plus a design margin before and after an edge (150 ps before a sample edge, one 50 ps grid step more; 105 ps after an idle edge moved 5 ps early), a busy re-arm, a reset after one decision with a start inside it, a reset while done is high and a start held high

name: sweep
purpose: irregular clock (4.05 ns to 9 ns between edges; the shortest periods are 4 ns plus one 50 ps grid step as a design margin); 34 back-to-back conversions, each started 2*tr plus one 50 ps grid step after the previous done edge: samples 4 mV below and above every DAC level 1..15 in mixed order, plus 0.02 V, 0.88 V, -0.1 V and 0.95 V; vin moves 0.3 V away 1 ns after each sample edge; all 16 codes

name: busy-reset
purpose: 7 ns clock, no power-up reset: a start before the first edge; re-arming while armed, after the sample edge and after one, two and three decisions (each abandoned conversion never publishes); resets after the sample edge, after three decisions, while done is high and while armed; a start request inside a reset that covers clock edges; a start 0.4 ns after the release

name: vss-override
purpose: vss 0.1 V, vref 0.9 V, vdd 1.2 V, vth 0.3 V, tr 100 ps (user decision A, 2026-10-28): the decision-card example 0.52 V gives code 8 (DAC(8) = 0.50 V; the span reading gives 7, the old public formula 9); a sample 30 mV above vss; samples below vss and above vref; a start, a clk pulse and a rst pulse that reach only 0.4 V and act for vth 0.3 V only

name: modules-override
purpose: the module tests with vss 0.1 V, vref 1.0 V, vdd 1.2 V, vth 0.3 V, tr 100 ps; a DAC bit, a sample_en pulse, a start, a cmp_i level and a rst pulse that reach only 0.4 V and act for vth 0.3 V only

name: reset-recovery-long-tr
purpose: tr = 1 ns (the upper end), 6 ns clock: a conversion of 0.60 V (code 10); a start request, then a 750 ps reset whose rising crossing is 2*tr plus a 9.375 ps design margin before the next clock edge (the reset-recovery limit; a separation exactly at it is a tie), with vin at 0.75 V there: the controller is idle, so that edge samples nothing and sample_dbg stays at vss; a conversion of 0.30 V (code 5); a conversion abandoned by a reset 2*tr plus 9.375 ps before an edge after its first decision; a start request followed by a reset 250 ps before the next clock edge that covers it (sample_en still high there); a conversion of 0.85 V (code 15) and a reset 2*tr plus 9.375 ps before an edge while done is high

name: modules-initial
purpose: the DAC and the comparator on their own, default parameters, from input-dependent initial states: the DAC bits start at code 11 (bit_3, bit_1, bit_0 high) and the comparator difference at -0.15 V (cmp_o low at t = 0); then DAC codes 9, 6, 15, 0, 11, 4, 13 with multi-bit changes and comparator crossings in both directions
